analyst_view.overall: Shakhtar (21st, 4 points) host Fenerbahce (19th, 5 points) at Stamford Bridge in London because of the war, so there is little real home advantage; both need points to stay in play-off contention, and Arda Turan said his side want to win and play with aggression and energy. Shakhtar are winless in three and miss Pedrinho and Gleiker Mendoza (ankle, out for the rest of 2026), Kaua Elias (leg fracture) and Marlon Santos, all now on the numbers' list, which cut Shakhtar's goals hard. Fenerbahce, under Emre Belozoglu, drew 2-2 at Kocaelispor; Turkish reports (Sporx citing TRT Spor, Ajansspor) have Kante back in midfield and Muriqi starting up front instead of Lukaku, with Ake (counted) and Asensio out. English referee Michael Oliver (4.0 cards a game) is named and already counted. Since this morning the numbers have taken in Elias, so my small cuts for him are gone and I stay with the numbers on every stat.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, only 0.8 of them Shakhtar's, because they already take Pedrinho (-14%) and Mendoza (-28%) off Shakhtar and list Elias too, while adding 6% for Ake missing at Fenerbahce's back. My earlier trim for Elias would now count twice, and Muriqi for Lukaku is a like-for-like swap, so I stay at 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already raised about 12% for Shakhtar's busy recent corner count and trimmed 9% for Fenerbahce's. A neutral ground in London takes some of Shakhtar's home push away, but Fenerbahce's wide players Greenwood and Akturkoglu and a target man in Muriqi keep crosses coming, so nothing points clearly either way and I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, a high figure that reflects Fenerbahce's card-heavy style and both sides' records, with referee Michael Oliver near the average at 4.0 a game. Two Turkish coaches with a Galatasaray-Fenerbahce history, Turan promising aggression and Kante's return add edge, but the numbers already carry that style, and Marlon Gomes being one booking from a ban may make him careful, so I stay at 4.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.4 shots, with Shakhtar's recent shooting run already adding about 15% to their side and Fenerbahce's trimmed 9%. Shakhtar's missing forwards show more in finishing than in volume, and Muriqi is a busier shooter than Lukaku has been lately, so I stay at about 26.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Without Elias and Mendoza, Shakhtar lean on Alisson Santana and young Luca Meirelles, but both absences are now on the numbers' list, so I drop my earlier small trim and stay at 8.8.
